digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate impact model and calibration (plan-v3 → plan-v4)
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis is miscalibrated: it fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings and has never been formally specified with worked examples, unlike its sibling ac_unverifiable; ~90% of the 1,307 'omitted scope site' class findings are graded none despite being the core class the axis exists to describe.

A G6 finding (c4ad-a93e-0613-408f) asserts a plan mechanism that would re-embed the entire corpus on container boot but scores impact=0.0 because all seven axes grade none; the real harms (prod_impact: medium, blast_radius: module, likelihood: medium) are unread by impact_plan since they belong to the superseded mean model.

The divergent_implementation axis must migrate from ordinal grades (none|low|medium|high) to a closed Literal set distinguishing load-bearing divergence (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site at 0.85 floor) from cosmetic omission (incomplete_enumeration below 0.60, never flooring), mirroring the oracle-kind precedent.

A structural change to impact_plan is required: divergent_implementation must be excluded from the generic _SEV01 contribution loop and resolved through a dedicated DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 map, preventing silent zero-scoring of the new symbolic grades.

High-cost LLM-based calibration assessments (purpose-built eval suites, bulk re-review runs) are rejected by ADR-0054 in favor of corpus replay and dogfooding; this narrows ADR-0036's A/B clause while preserving the permissive-rollout invariant and version-segmentation rules.

A prod_impact floor ('Fix 2') is rejected because it collides with the novelty_priority_floor=0.4 convergence mechanism: severity-band lifts are unbounded and non-remediable by plan edits, unlike semantic divergence classes, and would prevent loop termination.
